messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] verdant-prod streaming p99 latency breach detected — 3.2s (SLO 1.5s). paging on-call.
maya: on it, paging eng-oncall now. any customer impact reported yet?
oleg: I'm seeing a correlated jump in streaming stalls and a lot of long-prefix requests from a single tenant (verdant). p95 up too but p99 is worse.
sam: linking dashboards: https://dash.redwood/streams/verdant-prod?range=15m — look at the session-duration and stall-count graphs.
ivy: verdant on our dedicated pools? yes they have single-tenant reservation on gptx-large-dedicated-2.
maya: verdant admits there's a prompt-storm: many long chat histories being replayed (~10k tokens) plus concurrent sessions. they pushed a new client that retries on partial streams.
oleg: suspect KV cache thrash + memory pressure on the worker leads to stalls while we recompute KV caches for long prefixes.
sam: I see worker mem spikes and GC pauses in the same window. stack traces show repeated tokenizers and long attention matmuls.
nora: can we throttle client concurrency for verdant temporarily? we have per-tenant rate controls but their burst is within committed throughput.
maya: propose immediate mitigations: 1) enable conservative batching on verdant route 2) throttle new session creation to 50r/s 3) temporarily route highest-latency traffic to fallback smaller model (gptx-medium-quant).
oleg: running command to set route batching to conservative:
```bash
redwoodctl routes update verdant-prod --batching conservative
```
ivy: applied. confirmation: batching profile updated, effective ~30s.
sam: adding a temporary rate-limit override for policy check:
```bash
redwoodctl quota set verdant-prod --sessions-per-second 50 --duration 15m
```
maya: done. verdant notified of throttling via customer-notify flow.
runbook-bot: Refer to runbook 'streaming-tail-latency' — steps 1-4 executed: batching, throttle, fallback route. Continue monitoring.
oleg: spun up 2 extra capacity nodes on verdant-dedicated pool (auto-scale didn't kick due to commitment cap) with:
```bash
kubectl scale deployment/verdant-worker --replicas=8 -n inference-verdant
```
ivy: nodes accepted. pods starting; however one pod shows OOMKilled repeatedly — guessing model variant mismatch on quantization plugin.
sam: check pod logs:
```bash
kubectl logs verdant-worker-7 -n inference-verdant | tail -n 200
```
oleg: logs show repeated 'kv_cache_miss' and 'large_prefix_deserialize' errors around stall windows. also repeated `cuda out of memory` on smaller instance — quantization parameters not applied.
maya: temporary mitigation: add routing rule to send sessions with prompt length > 6k tokens to a non-streaming (batch generate) path to avoid streaming backpressure.
oleg: added rule. config snippet:
```json
{ "route": "verdant-prod", "match": {"prompt_tokens_gt":6000}, "action": {"mode": "batch", "model": "gptx-medium-quant"} }
```
ivy: rule active. macro effect: immediate drop in streaming stall count (observed ~2m after).
sam: alert flapping reduced. p95 dropped toward 1.1s, p99 still ~1.9s — improved but not at SLO.
maya: customer impact: verdant reports degraded tail latency and occasional truncated responses. they confirmed the new client retries amplified load.
oleg: collecting artifacts for postmortem: heap profiles, pprof, worker logs, route configs. saving to s3://incidents/verdant/6549873210/
runbook-bot: Artifact checklist: "heap", "pprof", "metrics_snapshot", "trace_sample" — marked collected: heap, metrics_snapshot, trace_sample.
nora: scheduling on-call handoff in 20m for deeper triage — @ivy you will take 2nd shift? can you lead the postmortem starter?
ivy: yes, I'll take handoff. will capture timeline and mitigation steps.
maya: prep note for customer success: summarize actions and ask verdant to roll-back client retry behavior. cc @nora.
oleg: follow-up actions: 1) fix quantization plugin mismatch causing OOM on scale-up 2) add long-prefix detection to routing and automatic batch-fallthrough 3) improve per-tenant concurrency safeguards 4) create regression test for long-prefix streaming.
sam: adding an alert tweak: raise the anomaly threshold for single-tenant long-prefix events to avoid noise but keep SLO-based paging.
runbook-bot: Runbook update queued: add step to auto-detect long-prefix patterns and recommend batch path. PR: https://git.redwood/runbooks/pull/124
ivy: handoff notes: timeline + commands + artifacts uploaded. I'll open postmortem doc and invite eng/infra/seqs.
maya: thanks team. keep channel for updates; if anything changes escalate.
oleg: leaving a final snapshot at last_message_ts, moving to handoff. :white_check_mark:
maya: acknowledged. closing page to on-call rotation. :thumbsup:
